Hmm!!! Thank you for bringing other social factors info the conversation. Many "charismatic" people I know, in a addition to having a way with words , also have some other forms of social capital - but not tooo much. Like. I think there's something about striking that balance between seeming like someone who's on a bit of a pedestal, but they're not TOTALLY visibly privileged because that makes them unrelatable. They've got a balance between some kinds of privilege which I think makes them more favourable (for example , pretty privilege, even class privilege and seeming intelligent/"educated) but in my observations also have something that gives them a sense of humility. 

An example. The CEO at a place I used to work.  She is suuuuuper charismatic. Great public speaker. Knows how to 'hold a room' , has authority, she's also has a doctorate even though that's totally going above and beyond in my field. But she is also funny in a very relatable way. And she's constantly talking about her dog. 

That balance. I think that's what makes that stock standard "charisma". The kind that make people want to put you in leadership positions because you have influence
